title: Read a chart in 3 steps
lines: 1. Sun, Moon and rising. 2. The houses. 3. The aspects between planets.
caption:
How to read a birth chart in 3 steps. ✦

◆ 1. Start with the big three: Sun (who you are), Moon (what you need), rising sign (how you meet the world)
◆ 2. Find the houses: the 12 areas of life, set by your rising sign
◆ 3. Look at the aspects: the angles between planets, which show how parts of you work together or pull apart

title: Sun, Moon and Rising
lines: Sun: who you are. Moon: what you need. Rising: how you meet the world.
caption:
Sun, Moon and rising: the big three of your chart. ✦

◆ Sun: your core identity and vitality
◆ Moon: your emotions, habits and what makes you feel safe
◆ Rising: the sign on the horizon at your birth, how others first meet you

One tells you who you are, one what you need, one how you arrive. Ask the Oracle for all three: link in bio.

title: Western and Vedic
lines: Western starts at the equinox; Vedic is fixed to the stars, about 24° apart.
caption:
Western or Vedic astrology? Within reads both. ✦

◆ Western (tropical): the zodiac starts at the spring equinox. It is strong on psychology and personal growth
◆ Vedic (sidereal): the zodiac is fixed to the stars, about 24° behind. It is strong on timing, with the Moon star (nakshatra) and life chapters (dasha)

That gap, the ayanamsa, is why your Vedic Sun sign can differ from your Western one.

title: Your Moon sign
lines: Your Moon is your inner weather: what you need to feel safe.
caption:
Your Moon sign is your inner weather. ☽

The Moon changes sign about every 2.5 days, so it is the fastest-moving part of your chart, and the one that shapes your needs and habits.

◆ Fire Moons (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius) tend to need action and appreciation
◆ Earth Moons (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn) tend to need steadiness and comfort
◆ Air Moons (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius) tend to need talk and space
◆ Water Moons (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces) tend to need depth and closeness

title: Why birth time matters
lines: Your rising sign changes about every two hours, and with it your houses.
caption:
Why your birth time matters. ✦

The rising sign changes about every two hours, and your houses are built from it. A few minutes can move a planet into a different house, and on some days the Moon can change sign.

If you know your birth time, the Oracle can read your houses and your rising sign. If you only know it roughly, it can still read your Sun and Moon.

title: What is a Saturn return?
lines: Saturn takes about 29.5 years to circle the zodiac: the first return is around 27 to 30.
caption:
What is a Saturn return? ♄

About every 29.5 years, Saturn comes back to the sign and degree it held when you were born. The first return falls around ages 27 to 30, the second around 58 to 60.

Astrologers read it as a time of review: what you have built, what holds up, what to commit to. Ask the Oracle where Saturn sits in your chart: link in bio.
